subject: HSS
title: Continuity and Change (Local History)
description: Third-grade history–social science focused on the student's own region: its physical geography, the American Indian nations who have lived there since long ago and today, the explorers, missions, ranchos and settlers who changed it, and how the local community was founded and has changed over time. Students also learn about rules, laws, citizenship and the three branches of government, national symbols and heroes, and the local economy, using maps, photographs, oral histories and other primary sources.
framework: California History–Social Science Content Standards; 2016 CA History–Social Science Framework

standards.3.1: Students describe the physical and human geography and use maps, tables, graphs, photographs and charts to organize information about people, places and environments in a spatial context.
standards.3.1.1: Identify geographical features in their local region (deserts, mountains, valleys, hills, coastal areas, oceans, lakes).
standards.3.1.2: Trace the ways in which people have used the resources of the local region and modified the physical environment (dams, cultivation, buildings).
standards.3.2: Students describe the American Indian nations in their local region long ago and in the recent past.
standards.3.2.1: Describe national identities, religious beliefs, customs and various folklore traditions of local American Indian nations.
standards.3.2.2: Discuss the ways in which physical geography, including climate, influenced how local Indian nations adapted to their natural environment (food, clothing, tools).
standards.3.2.3: Describe the economy and systems of government, particularly those with tribal constitutions, and their relationship to federal and state governments.
standards.3.2.4: Discuss the interaction of new settlers with the already established Indians of the region.
standards.3.3: Students draw from historical and community resources to organize the sequence of local historical events and describe how each period of settlement left its mark on the land.
standards.3.3.1: Research the explorers who visited here, the newcomers who settled here, and the people who continue to come to the region, including their cultural and religious traditions and contributions.
standards.3.3.2: Describe the economies established by settlers and their influence on the present-day economy, with emphasis on private property and entrepreneurship.
standards.3.3.3: Trace why their community was established, how individuals and families contributed to its founding and development, and how it has changed over time, drawing on maps, photographs, oral histories, letters, newspapers and other primary sources.
standards.3.4: Students understand the role of rules and laws in our daily lives and the basic structure of the U.S. government.
standards.3.4.1: Determine the reasons for rules, laws and the U.S. Constitution; the role of citizenship in promoting rules and laws; and the consequences for people who violate rules and laws.
standards.3.4.2: Discuss the importance of public virtue and the role of citizens, including how to participate in a classroom, in the community and in civic life.
standards.3.4.3: Know the histories of important local and national landmarks, symbols and essential documents that create a sense of community among citizens and exemplify cherished ideals (flag, bald eagle, Statue of Liberty, Constitution, Declaration of Independence, U.S. Capitol).
standards.3.4.4: Understand the three branches of government, with an emphasis on local government.
standards.3.4.5: Describe the ways in which California, the other states and sovereign American Indian tribes contribute to the making of our nation and participate in the federal system of government.
standards.3.4.6: Describe the lives of American heroes who took risks to secure our freedoms (e.g., Anne Hutchinson, Benjamin Franklin, Thomas Jefferson, Abraham Lincoln, Frederick Douglass, Harriet Tubman, Martin Luther King Jr.).
standards.3.5: Students demonstrate basic economic reasoning skills and an understanding of the economy of the local region.
standards.3.5.1: Describe the ways in which local producers have used and are using natural, human and capital resources to produce goods and services in the past and the present.
standards.3.5.2: Understand that some goods are made locally, some elsewhere in the United States and some abroad.
standards.3.5.3: Understand that individual economic choices involve trade-offs and the evaluation of benefits and costs.
standards.3.5.4: Discuss the relationship of students' 'work' in school and their personal human capital.

resources.name: Calisphere

resources.name: Library of Congress – Classroom Materials
resources.note: Primary source sets on symbols, the Constitution, maps and American heroes

resources.name: DocsTeach (National Archives)
resources.note: Primary documents and activities on the Constitution, Declaration and civic life

resources.name: Ben's Guide to the U.S. Government
resources.note: Kid-level explanations of the three branches, symbols and citizenship

resources.name: iCivics
resources.note: Free civics games and lessons on rules, laws and government

resources.name: Chronicling America (Library of Congress)
resources.note: Historic newspapers to research how your community has changed

units.title: Our Land: Geography of Our Region
units.big_idea: Landforms, water and climate shape where and how people live in our region.

units.title: The First Peoples of Our Region
units.big_idea: American Indian nations adapted to the land, built rich cultures and continue as sovereign nations today.

units.title: Newcomers: Explorers, Missions and Ranchos
units.big_idea: Explorers and settlers brought great change to the region and to its first peoples.

units.title: Building Our Community Over Time
units.big_idea: Every community has a story of founders, newcomers and change that we can uncover with primary sources.

units.title: Rules, Laws and Good Citizens
units.big_idea: Rules and laws protect people, and good citizens help their communities.

units.title: How Government Works
units.big_idea: Our government has three branches at local, state and national levels, and tribes are sovereign nations within the federal system.

units.title: American Symbols, Landmarks and Heroes
units.big_idea: Symbols, documents and heroes remind us of shared ideals like freedom and equality.

units.title: Our Local Economy
units.big_idea: People use resources to produce goods and services, and every economic choice has a trade-off.

units.title: Community History Showcase
units.big_idea: Historians share what they learn so others can understand their community.

objectives: Use map elements (title, compass rose, key, scale)
Locate our community on maps

days.title: Map parts
days.work: Identify title, compass rose, map key and scale on a printed local map.

days.title: Where in the world
days.work: Locate your continent, country, state and city on a globe and make a 'nested circles' address.

days.title: Grid maps
days.work: Use a grid to locate places on a town map and give directions using cardinal directions.

days.title: Draw a map
days.work: Draw a map of your neighborhood with a key and compass rose.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a map skills quiz and explain your neighborhood map.

objectives: Identify landforms and water features in the local region

days.title: Landform vocabulary
days.work: Define and sketch 10 landforms and water bodies.

days.title: California regions
days.work: Locate the coast, Central Valley, Sierra Nevada and desert regions on a physical map.

days.title: Local features
days.work: Identify the landforms and water near your town using a local physical map.

days.title: Salt dough map
days.work: Build a salt dough relief map of your region showing main landforms.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Label a blank map of your region and describe its features.

objectives: Describe local climate and natural resources

days.title: Climate
days.work: Describe the climate of your region using temperature and rainfall data.

days.title: Resources
days.work: List local natural resources (water, soil, timber, minerals, fish).

days.title: Water source
days.work: Research where your town's drinking water comes from.

days.title: Resource map
days.work: Make a resource map with symbols.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write how one resource is important to your community.

objectives: Trace how people have modified the local environment

days.title: Then and now
days.work: Compare historic and current photos of your region from Calisphere.

days.title: Dams and aqueducts
days.work: Learn about a California dam or aqueduct and its effects.

days.title: Farming
days.work: Explore how irrigation changed the Central Valley.

days.title: Cause and effect
days.work: Make a chart of human changes to the land and their effects.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about one positive and one negative environmental change.

objectives: Observe local geography firsthand
Present geographic findings

days.title: Field trip
days.work: Visit a local park, river or hill and sketch landforms and plants.

days.title: Human features
days.work: Identify roads, buildings and bridges in the area.

days.title: Field map
days.work: Make a map of the field study site.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present findings with photos.

days.title: Unit 1 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on geography.

objectives: Identify the American Indian nations of the local region
Locate homelands on a map

days.title: Tribal map
days.work: Locate your region's original peoples on a California Indian territories map (e.g., Ohlone, Chumash, Miwok, Tongva, Kumeyaay, Yokuts).

days.title: Land acknowledgment
days.work: Learn whose land you live on and write a land acknowledgment.

days.title: Living cultures
days.work: Visit a local tribe's official website to learn about its present-day community.

days.title: Language
days.work: Learn a few words from a local tribal language if available.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write facts about the local nation then and now.

objectives: Describe how geography influenced food, clothing, shelter and tools

days.title: Food
days.work: Learn how acorns were gathered, leached and ground; look at photos of grinding stones.

days.title: Shelter
days.work: Compare tule, redwood bark and plank houses by region.

days.title: Clothing and tools
days.work: Study Calisphere photographs of tools and basketry.

days.title: Model
days.work: Build a model shelter from natural materials.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how geography shaped daily life.

objectives: Describe customs, beliefs and stories of local nations

days.title: Oral tradition
days.work: Read or listen to a California Indian story (e.g., a Coyote story) and discuss its lesson.

days.title: Ceremonies
days.work: Learn about a traditional ceremony and its meaning.

days.title: Basketry
days.work: Study California Indian basketry and its significance.

days.title: Compare
days.work: Compare a California Indian story to an Aesop fable.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about a tradition still practiced today.

weeks.topic: Trade and economy of first peoples
objectives: Describe how local nations traded and used resources
Compare traditional and modern tribal economies

days.title: Trade networks
days.work: Read about California Indian trade networks and trace a route on a map from the coast to the mountains.

days.title: Shell bead money
days.work: Learn how the Chumash made and used shell bead money and why it was valuable inland.

days.title: Barter game
days.work: Play a barter simulation trading household 'resources' (acorns, obsidian, shells, baskets) with family members.

days.title: Then and now
days.work: Compare traditional trade with a present-day tribal business or enterprise from a tribe's website.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining how trade helped communities get what their land did not provide.

objectives: Describe tribal governments and constitutions and their relationship to state and federal governments

days.title: Tribal council
days.work: Read how a local tribe's council is elected and what decisions it makes.

days.title: Constitution
days.work: Read short excerpts from a published tribal constitution and identify who can vote and what leaders do.

days.title: Sovereignty
days.work: Discuss what it means that tribes are sovereign nations with their own governments.

days.title: Relationships
days.work: Make a 3-column chart of tribal, state and federal government responsibilities.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer 6 questions about tribal government and explain one in a complete paragraph.

objectives: Discuss how newcomers and local Indian nations interacted
Recognize resilience

days.title: Arrival
days.work: Read about the arrival of Spanish, Mexican and American newcomers and list changes each brought.

days.title: Perspectives
days.work: Compare a settler's account and a Native account of the same period and note differences.

days.title: Changes
days.work: Chart changes to land, food, language and daily life for local nations.

days.title: Resilience
days.work: Learn how local nations have kept languages, ceremonies and basketry alive today.

days.title: Unit 2 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on local American Indian nations and present one fact you will remember.

objectives: Research explorers who visited the region
Analyze an early map
materials: Library of Congress early California maps

days.title: Cabrillo
days.work: Read about Juan Rodríguez Cabrillo's 1542 voyage and trace his route along the California coast.

days.title: Portolá and Crespí
days.work: Read about the 1769 Portolá expedition and an excerpt from Father Crespí's diary describing the land.

days.title: Early map
days.work: Examine an early map of California from the Library of Congress and note what mapmakers got right and wrong (e.g., California as an island).

days.title: Explorer card
days.work: Make an explorer trading card with dates, route, goals and effects on local people.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the explorer card and answer questions about the explorer's impact.

objectives: Describe the mission system and its effects on Native peoples

days.title: Three institutions
days.work: Learn the purposes of missions, presidios and pueblos and sort facts about each.

days.title: Nearest mission
days.work: Locate the mission nearest your home on a map and research when and why it was founded.

days.title: Native experience
days.work: Read about how mission life changed the work, diet, health and culture of Native peoples.

days.title: Photo analysis
days.work: Analyze a historic Calisphere photograph of a mission with a see-think-wonder chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining how the missions changed the region and its first peoples.

objectives: Describe the rancho economy and its legacy

days.title: Ranchos
days.work: Read about Mexican land grants, ranchos and the work of vaqueros.

days.title: Diseños
days.work: Examine a hand-drawn rancho map (diseño) on Calisphere and identify landmarks used as boundaries.

days.title: Hide and tallow
days.work: Learn how cattle hides and tallow were traded with ships and what was bought in return.

days.title: Place names
days.work: Find rancho or Spanish place names on a local map and research one name's origin.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in writing how the rancho economy worked and what names or traditions remain.

objectives: Research newcomers who settled the region and their contributions
materials: Gold Rush photographs and letters (Calisphere, Library of Congress)

days.title: Gold Rush
days.work: Learn how the 1848 gold discovery brought people from around the world to California.

days.title: Immigrant communities
days.work: Read about Chinese, Mexican, Chilean and African American Gold Rush communities and their contributions.

days.title: Primary source
days.work: Analyze a miner's letter or daguerreotype and write 3 observations and 2 questions.

days.title: Timeline
days.work: Build a timeline of newcomers to your region from first peoples to today.

days.title: Unit 3 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on explorers, missions, ranchos and settlers.

objectives: Trace why the community was established and who founded it

days.title: Founding
days.work: Research when and why your town was founded (railroad, farming, port, mining) using the historical society website.

days.title: Founders
days.work: Read about 2 founding individuals or families and their contributions.

days.title: Old maps
days.work: Compare a historic map of your town (Sanborn fire insurance map or USGS topo) with a current map.

days.title: Timeline
days.work: Begin a community timeline with founding events and dates.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining why your community began where it did.

objectives: Distinguish primary and secondary sources
Use them to trace change

days.title: Primary vs. secondary
days.work: Sort 10 sources (diary, textbook, photo, encyclopedia, letter) into primary and secondary.

days.title: Photo analysis
days.work: Analyze 3 historic photos of your town using a see-think-wonder chart.

days.title: Newspapers
days.work: Read a short historic newspaper article about your area on Chronicling America.

days.title: Then and now
days.work: Take a photo of the same spot as a historic picture and compare them.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write what changed and what stayed the same, citing both photos.

objectives: Plan and conduct an oral history interview

days.title: Questions
days.work: Write 10 open-ended interview questions for an older relative or neighbor about how the community has changed.

days.title: Interview
days.work: Conduct and record the interview, listening and asking follow-up questions.

days.title: Notes
days.work: Listen to the recording and take notes on the 5 most important details.

days.title: Share
days.work: Share 3 interesting stories from the interview with family.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a one-page summary of the oral history and add key events to the timeline.

objectives: Describe economies established by settlers and their influence today

days.title: Early businesses
days.work: Research 3 early businesses in your town (general store, mill, farm, cannery).

days.title: Entrepreneur
days.work: Read about a local entrepreneur and the risks they took to start a business.

days.title: Private property
days.work: Discuss why owning land and businesses encouraged settlers to build and invest.

days.title: Then and now
days.work: Compare early industries with today's major employers in a T-chart.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain in writing how one early business shaped today's local economy.

objectives: Create an illustrated community history timeline

days.title: Organize
days.work: Organize events from the unit into eras on a poster timeline.

days.title: Images
days.work: Add copies of photos, maps and newspaper clippings with captions.

days.title: Land changes
days.work: Add notes on how the land changed in each era (farms, roads, dams, buildings).

days.title: Present
days.work: Present the timeline to family, explaining 3 turning points.

days.title: Unit 4 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on community history and primary sources.

weeks.topic: Why we have rules and laws
objectives: Determine reasons for rules and laws
Explain consequences

days.title: Rules at home
days.work: List family rules and explain the reason behind each one.

days.title: Rules vs. laws
days.work: Compare rules and laws and sort examples (bedtime, speed limits, library fines).

days.title: Consequences
days.work: Discuss what consequences for breaking laws are meant to do (protect, teach, repair).

days.title: No-rules game
days.work: Play a ball game with no rules, then add rules and discuss how the game changed.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph about why communities need rules and laws.

objectives: Explain the purposes of the Constitution and the Bill of Rights

days.title: Preamble
days.work: Read the Preamble from the National Archives website and paraphrase each phrase in kid-friendly words.

days.title: Why it was written
days.work: Learn why the founders wrote the Constitution in 1787.

days.title: Bill of Rights
days.work: Read a kid-friendly summary of the Bill of Rights and pick the 3 rights you think matter most.

days.title: Family constitution
days.work: Write a family constitution with a preamble and 5 articles.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer questions on the Constitution and explain your family constitution.

objectives: Discuss citizens' responsibilities
Carry out community service

days.title: Citizens
days.work: Define citizenship and list rights and responsibilities of citizens.

days.title: Civic virtues
days.work: Discuss honesty, respect, responsibility and courage with real examples.

days.title: Plan a service project
days.work: Plan a small service project (park cleanup, food drive, cards for seniors).

days.title: Serve
days.work: Carry out the service project with family.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a reflection on how the project helped the community.

weeks.topic: Making a difference in civic life
objectives: Participate in civic life by voicing ideas and voting

days.title: Community issues
days.work: Identify a local issue (crosswalk safety, park repairs, litter) by observing your neighborhood.

days.title: Letter to an official
days.work: Write a polite letter to a city council member about the issue with a suggested solution.

days.title: Family vote
days.work: Hold a family vote on a real decision using secret ballots and count the majority.

days.title: Change makers
days.work: Read about a kid who made a difference in their community and discuss how.

days.title: Unit 5 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on rules, laws and citizenship.

objectives: Explain the legislative, executive and judicial branches and checks and balances

days.title: Branches
days.work: Use Ben's Guide to learn what each branch does and who works in it.

days.title: Checks and balances
days.work: Play a role game where one branch makes, one carries out and one judges a family 'law.'

days.title: National leaders
days.work: Identify the current President, your members of Congress and the Supreme Court.

days.title: Three-branch chart
days.work: Make a tree chart of the three branches with jobs and leaders.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer questions on the branches and explain why power is divided.

objectives: Describe local and state government roles

days.title: City government
days.work: Look up your mayor or city manager and council members on the city website and list their jobs.

days.title: Local services
days.work: List services local government provides (police, fire, parks, libraries) and who pays for them.

days.title: State government
days.work: Learn about the governor, the legislature and the State Capitol in Sacramento.

days.title: Council meeting
days.work: Watch 15 minutes of a recorded city council meeting and note one decision made.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a comparison chart of local, state and national government.

weeks.topic: States and tribes in the federal system
objectives: Describe how California, other states and tribes participate in the federal system

days.title: Federal system
days.work: Learn what the federal government does and what states do.

days.title: California's role
days.work: Find California's senators and representatives and explain how they represent us.

days.title: Tribal nations
days.work: Learn how sovereign tribes govern themselves and work with state and federal governments.

days.title: Map
days.work: Label California, neighboring states and California tribal lands on a map.

days.title: Unit 6 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on government.

objectives: Know the histories of national symbols and what ideals they represent
materials: symbol images from Library of Congress

days.title: Flag
days.work: Learn the history and meaning of the stars and stripes and the Pledge of Allegiance.

days.title: Bald eagle
days.work: Learn why the bald eagle was chosen as a national symbol and how it was saved from extinction.

days.title: Statue of Liberty
days.work: Learn the history of the Statue of Liberty and read lines from Emma Lazarus's 'The New Colossus.'

days.title: Liberty Bell
days.work: Learn the story of the Liberty Bell and the words inscribed on it.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Make a symbols booklet with a picture and the ideal each symbol represents.

objectives: Know histories of landmarks and essential documents

days.title: Declaration
days.work: Examine the Declaration of Independence and discuss 'all men are created equal' and 'unalienable rights.'

days.title: U.S. Capitol
days.work: Learn the history of the U.S. Capitol and what happens there.

days.title: California symbols
days.work: Learn the California flag, grizzly bear, poppy and state motto 'Eureka.'

days.title: Local landmark
days.work: Research a local landmark (historic building, statue or park) and its history.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the local landmark with a drawing and 5 facts.

weeks.topic: American heroes: founders and freedom seekers
objectives: Describe the lives of American heroes who took risks to secure freedoms

days.title: Benjamin Franklin
days.work: Learn about Franklin's role in independence and read 3 sayings from Poor Richard's Almanack.

days.title: Thomas Jefferson
days.work: Learn about Jefferson writing the Declaration of Independence.

days.title: Frederick Douglass
days.work: Read an adapted excerpt from Douglass's Narrative about learning to read and discuss the risk he took.

days.title: Harriet Tubman
days.work: Learn about Harriet Tubman's escape and Underground Railroad journeys.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph about the risk one hero took and why it mattered.

objectives: Describe heroes who advanced freedom and equality
Analyze speeches

days.title: Abraham Lincoln
days.work: Read the Gettysburg Address and discuss its message of 'a new birth of freedom.'

days.title: Martin Luther King Jr.
days.work: Read an excerpt of 'I Have a Dream' and list the dreams he describes.

days.title: Anne Hutchinson
days.work: Learn how Anne Hutchinson stood up for religious freedom.

days.title: Hero report
days.work: Write a one-page report on a chosen hero with a portrait.

days.title: Unit 7 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on symbols, documents and heroes.

objectives: Describe natural, human and capital resources used by local producers

days.title: Resources
days.work: Sort picture cards into natural, human and capital resources.

days.title: Goods and services
days.work: Sort 20 local jobs into producers of goods and providers of services.

days.title: Local producer
days.work: Visit or research a local farm, bakery or factory and list the resources it uses.

days.title: Production chart
days.work: Make a flow chart showing how a local product is made from resources to store.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Explain how a local producer uses all three kinds of resources, past and present.

objectives: Identify goods made locally, elsewhere in the U.S. and abroad

days.title: Label hunt
days.work: Check labels on 20 household items and record where each was made.

days.title: Map
days.work: Place dots on a world map for each item's origin and count local, national and foreign goods.

days.title: Local goods
days.work: Visit a farmers market and list goods made or grown locally.

days.title: Why trade
days.work: Discuss why we buy goods from other places (cost, climate, specialization).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about one item's journey from where it was made to your home.

objectives: Understand trade-offs and opportunity cost in economic choices

days.title: Scarcity
days.work: Discuss why we can't have everything we want (limited money, time).

days.title: Trade-offs

days.title: Opportunity cost
days.work: Identify the opportunity cost in 5 scenario cards (e.g., playing outside vs. watching a show).

days.title: Party budget
days.work: Plan a birthday party with a $50 budget, comparing costs and benefits of choices.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write about a real trade-off you made and its opportunity cost.

objectives: Relate learning in school to personal human capital

days.title: Human capital
days.work: Define human capital as the skills and knowledge people bring to work.

days.title: Skills
days.work: List skills you have built in school this year and how each could be used in a job.

days.title: Career interview
days.work: Interview a family member about the skills their job requires and how they learned them.

days.title: Goals
days.work: Set 2 learning goals for next year that build your human capital.

days.title: Unit 8 assessment
days.work: Complete the unit test on resources, trade, choices and human capital.

objectives: Share learning about the community through a museum exhibit

days.title: Plan
days.work: Plan a 'Museum of Our Community' with sections for geography, first peoples, settlement, government and economy.

days.title: Build
days.work: Build exhibits from the year's maps, timeline, oral history and reports with labels.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Rehearse a docent tour script explaining each exhibit.

days.title: Showcase
days.work: Host the museum for family and friends and lead tours.

days.title: Reflection
days.work: Write a reflection on how your community has changed and what has stayed the same.
